text:
Alex Chen: quick check — I'm updating the API contract for auth behavior. How should we handle requests that have an org-scoped API key but no X-Project-Id header?

Maria Gomez: we currently allow org-scoped keys to succeed without X-Project-Id (treated as org-level access). project-scoped keys require X-Project-Id to match.

Samir Patel: can we agree on the response codes mapping? my understanding: missing auth -> 401, malformed/invalid key -> 401, valid key but lacking project access -> 403. Saw a client get 403 for expired token though.

Luis Ortega: correct mapping today is what Samir described. the 403-for-expired was a bug in the token-validation layer (returned forbidden instead of unauthorized). fixed in staging but worth adding tests.

Alex Chen: also need to decide on header precedence and legacy support. we still get calls using `X-Api-Key` and some proxies strip `Authorization`. Proposal: precedence = Authorization: Bearer > X-Api-Key (legacy) > SDK-injected project header. keep `X-Api-Key` supported for 6 months with clear deprecation warnings.

Maria Gomez: agreed. will add deprecation window and an examples section. sample header patterns I plan to include:

```
# org-scoped key, inferred org usage
Authorization: Bearer <ORG_KEY>
# project-scoped key with explicit project header
Authorization: Bearer <PROJECT_KEY>
X-Project-Id: proj_123
# legacy header we still accept
X-Api-Key: <KEY>
```

Samir Patel: +1. i'll add unit/integration tests for these combos. Also propose canonical error bodies so clients can code against error codes rather than message strings. e.g. 401 -> {"error":{"code":"AUTH_MISSING","message":...}}; 403 -> {"error":{"code":"AUTH_FORBIDDEN"}}

Luis Ortega: one compatibility note — some customers use edge proxies that lowercase headers or drop Authorization. we should accept both `x-api-key` and `X-Api-Key` (case-insensitive already by HTTP) and document an SDK fallback to send legacy header when `Authorization` is absent.

Alex Chen: agreed. also, for key rotation we added a very short grace behavior recently where rotated keys may still pass and we return an `X-Auth-Warn` header. do we want to keep that? it complicates client semantics.

Maria Gomez: i think we should keep rotation transparent but not change success/failure semantics. the warn header is useful for observability but clients shouldn't rely on it. i'll document it under observability, not contract.

Samir Patel: action items: I'll add integration tests (org_key/project_key/expired/revoked combos) and a test that verifies 401 vs 403 mapping.

Luis Ortega: I'll scan infra for proxies that might strip Authorization and list affected customers. will also add a note in the deploy checklist.

Maria Gomez: I'll update the API contract doc (endpoints + header precedence + error body schema) and add the deprecation schedule for `X-Api-Key`. i'll also include sample curl snippets and SDK guidance.

Alex Chen: add one more: standardize error codes: AUTH_MISSING, AUTH_INVALID, AUTH_FORBIDDEN, AUTH_EXPIRED. return `request_id` in all error responses for traceability.

Maria Gomez: noted — will include mapping table and sample curl tests.

Luis Ortega: small ask — confirm caching behavior: if we route to fallback model variant due to capacity but auth is valid, we should not change auth checks or mask scope in caches. auth must be evaluated before any model fallback logic.

Alex Chen: yes, auth first, routing second. thanks. i'll open a meta PR linking Maria's doc updates + Samir's tests + Luis's infra checklist. ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout to beta finished for service/auth-service v1.42.3 — no auth regressions observed in smoke tests.
